title: Participle Clauses
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! El uso de las 'Participle Clauses' es la marca de un escritor magistral en inglés. Al comprimir oraciones largas en cláusulas concisas usando 'Having + participio' o 'V-ing', logras un tono ejecutivo, eficiente e increíblemente profesional.

parts.visual:
En el nivel C2, usamos 'Participle Clauses' para hacer nuestra escritura más eficiente y fluida, combinando dos oraciones que tienen el mismo sujeto. 

1. Present Participle (-ing): Expresa causa o dos cosas pasando al mismo tiempo. 
Normal: Because he realized the danger, he canceled the project. 
Participle Clause: REALIZING the danger, he canceled the project. 

2. Perfect Participle (Having + Past Participle): Expresa que una acción terminó ANTES de que empezara la otra. 
Normal: After she had reviewed the report, she signed it. 
Participle Clause: HAVING REVIEWED the report, she signed it.
parts.audio: Welcome to Participle Clauses. In the C2 level, we use these to make our writing more efficient by combining two sentences with the same subject. Number 1: Present Participle, using 'ing'. It expresses a cause or two things happening at the same time. Normal sentence: Because he realized the danger, he canceled the project. With a Participle Clause: REALIZING the danger, he canceled the project. Number 2: Perfect Participle, using 'Having' plus a Past Participle. It expresses that one action finished BEFORE the other started. Normal: After she had reviewed the report, she signed it. Participle Clause: HAVING REVIEWED the report, she signed it.

parts.visual:
3. Past Participle (-ed / 3ra columna): Tiene un significado pasivo (algo fue hecho al sujeto). 
Normal: Because the CEO was driven by ambition, he took huge risks. 
Participle Clause: DRIVEN by ambition, the CEO took huge risks. 

4. Formas Negativas: Ponemos 'Not' ANTES del participio. 
Ej: NOT KNOWING what to do, I called my lawyer. (Because I didn't know...) 
Ej: NOT HAVING RECEIVED the funds, we delayed the launch. (Because we hadn't received...) 

Importante: ¡El sujeto debe ser el mismo en ambas partes de la oración para evitar el error del 'Dangling Participle'!
parts.audio: Number 3: Past Participle, which has a passive meaning. Normal: Because the CEO was driven by ambition, he took huge risks. Participle Clause: DRIVEN by ambition, the CEO took huge risks. Number 4: Negative forms. We put 'Not' BEFORE the participle. For example: NOT KNOWING what to do, I called my lawyer. Or: NOT HAVING RECEIVED the funds, we delayed the launch. Very important: The subject must be exactly the same in both parts of the sentence to avoid a Dangling Participle error!

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Transforma o elige la cláusula correcta.

questions.question: Normal: Because he hoped to secure the contract, he offered a 10% discount. -> ____ to secure the contract, he offered a 10% discount.
Normal: After we had signed the agreement, we celebrated with champagne. -> ____ the agreement, we celebrated with champagne.
questions.explanation: Having signed (acción terminada antes de la celebración).

questions.question: Normal: Because it was built in 1920, the factory needs extensive renovations. -> ____ in 1920, the factory needs extensive renovations.
Normal: Because she didn't want to offend the client, she agreed to the changes. -> ____ to offend the client, she agreed to the changes.
____ the full instructions, the intern made several costly mistakes. (Como no había leído...)
questions.explanation: Not having read (negación de una acción pasada perfecta).

questions.question: ____ by the sudden drop in profits, the CEO called an emergency meeting. (Alarmado por...)
____ in London for ten years, he speaks with a British accent. (Habiendo vivido...)
questions.explanation: Having lived (acción terminada o experiencia acumulada).

questions.question: ____ out of money, the startup was forced to shut down. (Habiéndose quedado sin dinero...)
questions.explanation: Having run out of money (acción completada antes del cierre).

questions.question: ____ that the market was unstable, we decided to wait before investing. (Sabiendo que...)
____ at the hotel, they immediately checked their emails. (Al llegar...)
questions.explanation: Arriving (dos acciones casi simultáneas) o Having arrived. 'Arriving' es común y correcto aquí.

questions.question: ____ in a high-interest account, the money grew quickly. (Invertido en...)
____ the necessary skills, she wasn't hired for the job. (Al no poseer...)
____ an MBA from Harvard, she was highly sought after by recruiters. (Teniendo un MBA...)
____ by the scandal, the politician resigned. (Destruido por...)
____ the email, he realized he had made a terrible mistake. (Después de haber enviado...)
____ all day, the committee finally reached a verdict. (Habiendo deliberado...)
¿Cuál es un 'Dangling Participle' (error gramatical)?
options: Walking down the street, the building caught my eye.
Walking down the street, I saw the building.
Having finished the report, she left the office.
questions.correct_answer: Walking down the street, the building caught my eye.
questions.explanation: Es un error porque implica que el edificio ('the building') era el que estaba caminando.

questions.question: ____ how to proceed, they hired a consultant. (Sin saber...)
____ to a senior position, he now has his own office. (Habiendo sido promovido...)
____ off his debt, he felt a great sense of relief. (Habiendo pagado...)

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra o palabras de la cláusula.

questions.question: After he signed -> ____ signed the deal, he left.
Because she realized -> ____ the danger, she ran.
Because it was built in 1990 -> ____ in 1990, it is old.
Because I didn't know -> ____ knowing what to do...
Because we hadn't received -> Not ____ received the funds...
Because he hoped -> ____ to win, he practiced.
Because he was alarmed -> ____ by the news, he called.
After they finished -> ____ finished the meeting, they ate.
Because I didn't want to -> ____ wanting to fight...
Because she had lived there -> ____ lived there, she knew the city.
